goal: Integrate the WHO Life_Expectancy_Data, the UCI Cleveland heart cohort, World Bank life expectancy and income groups, and CDC BRFSS state obesity data. The work covers a US macro-vs-clinical memo with discrepancies, PCA burden score with country clustering, name reconciliation, a mixed-effects vs pooled OLS model, and an income-adjusted obesity ranking with WLS. Deliver a notebook, Integrated_Analysis_Report.xlsx (4 sheets) and a 2-page PDF brief.
delivered: Integrated_Health_Analysis.ipynb, Integrated_Analysis_Report.xlsx (Country_Clusters, Name_Reconciliation_Log, Mixed_Model_Results, Adjusted_Obesity_Rankings) and the 2-page Cross_Level_Health_Analysis.pdf. They cover 3-PC PCA with k=3 k-means by silhouette, a 2,304-row merged panel, a mixed model with LR test, ACS-income-standardized obesity rankings for 51 states with 42 shifting at least 3 places, and HC3 WLS.
what_went_wrong: The agent never audited the US rows of Life_Expectancy_Data.csv year by year. It missed the BMI scale anomaly (6.1/6.9 in 2000-01 vs 61.7-69.6 later) and the Adult Mortality 10x drop (111-115 to 11-18 after 2006), and used both uncritically: the US mean, PCA inputs, and the mixed model where adult_mortality -1.74 is a 'key predictor'. PCA was hard-coded to n_components=3 with no scree, Kaiser or cumulative-variance justification, and k-means was never justified against hierarchical clustering. For obesity, latest_question() silently took Tennessee's 2023 value (37.6) into the 2024 ranking without flagging it.

failed_items.why: The staged CSV has US BMI 6.1, 6.9, then 61.7-69.6, but the notebook only renames BMI and uses it as a model covariate. The PDF says only that 'WHO BMI ... are country aggregates', with no scale or data-entry diagnosis. The ecological-mismatch sub-criterion passed.

PCA(n_components=3) is hard-coded. Explained-variance ratios appear only as biplot axis labels, and there is no scree, Kaiser or cumulative-variance retention rule. Subset choice, missingness handling, scaling and the biplot all passed.

k=3 was chosen by silhouette and labels were given, but the choice of k-means over hierarchical clustering is never argued. The notebook has no 'hierarch' mention, and the PDF says only 'K-means selected k=3 by the largest silhouette (0.55)'.

latest_question() takes each state's most recent non-null year, so Tennessee enters the 2024 ranking with 2023 data ('TN,Tennessee,2023,37.6'). The PDF and notebook never disclose the missing 2024 TN value.

US Adult Mortality is 111-115 in 2000-06 and 11-18 in 2007-15 in the staged file. The code averages it (us_who.adult_mortality.mean()) and feeds it to PCA and mixedlm without any year-level check, and the PDF reports adult_mortality -1.74 as a top predictor with no anomaly note.
